coverSub: Spot the type before you plan — it decides your whole structure.
s2c1b: Agree, disagree, or partly agree — and defend one clear position throughout.
s2c2b: Discuss both sides fairly and give your own opinion — in the introduction, and again in the conclusion.
s2c3b: Weigh benefits against drawbacks — including "outweigh" questions.
s3c1b: Explain why something happens and what could realistically fix it.
s3c2b: Answer one, two, or three separate questions directly — don't merge them into one.
s3c3h: The same topic, a different type
s3c3b: IELTS uses its topics again and again, and the same subject — art funding, say — can come back as an Opinion, a Discussion or a Direct Question essay. Read the instruction line every time, never just the topic.
q1Expl: A direct "do you agree" question — this is an Opinion essay.
q2Expl: "Discuss both sides" is the signal phrase for a Discussion essay.
q3Expl: "Benefits and drawbacks" is asking you to weigh advantages against disadvantages.
q4Expl: Causes plus a fix requested — the classic shape of a Cause / Problem / Solution essay.
q5Expl: This asks you to answer one specific question directly — a Direct Question essay, not a broad discussion of both sides.
q6Expl: Again, "discuss both views" marks this as a Discussion essay.
q7Expl: "To what extent do you agree" asks for your position directly — Opinion.
q8Expl: "Why" plus "what measures" — reasons and a fix, so Cause / Problem / Solution.
q9Expl: "Advantages and disadvantages" — weigh both sides of the same trend.
q10Expl: Two separate questions to answer directly — a Direct Question essay, not a single agree/disagree position.
